paragraphs: R’ Levi Tzanavriya. (The name of a city, as in [Megillah, chapter 3, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.3.1.10).)

He is mentioned in [Sheviit, chapter 6, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.6.2.4), where he asked R’ Yitzchak and R’ Immi; and there, [chapter 9, halakhah 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sheviit.9.5.8), he asked R’ Ba bar Zavda (the Zhitomir printing has simply “R’ Levi”). In [Avodah Zarah, end of chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.9.7): “Levi Tzanavriya’s servant boy was selling produce” [the matching passage; supplied מלויא … מוכן differs]. Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha reports in Rabbi Yasa’s name: “The servant of a trustworthy person is like the trustworthy person.” Hyman explains: his young men were selling produce under the presumption that it had been tithed. [Avodah Zarah 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.39a.13) brings something similar about R’ Levi’s servant; see his entry.

notes.text: The translation of the servant’s activity follows the linked Yerushalmi passage, which reads “was selling produce.” The supplied wording is discussed below.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2352&lang=en) also names the sages whom Levi asked in the two Sheviit passages. It assigns the second question to chapter 9, halakhah 7. Hyman’s halakhah 5 agrees with the numbering of the linked edition.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 864) reads טלייא, a boy, where the supplied Hebrew has מלויא, and it also reads מוכן where the consulted Venice Yerushalmi has מזבן, selling. Hyman’s own gloss says the young men sold produce presumed tithed. Both consulted Sheviit passages name Levi with the place epithet and give the same questioned sages as Hyman. Megillah 3:1 mentions the Torah scroll of the people of Tzanavriya in the Ursicinus episode. The Zhitomir reading remains Hyman’s report. In the Bavli’s example at Avodah Zarah 39a, the servant used to sell asafoetida, and those who consulted Rabbi Yochanan asked whether they could still buy from him after Rabbi Levi’s death. The parallel does not establish a shared identity.
